recipes.name: Picnic Potato Salad with No Mayonnaise

steps.text: Place potatoes in a large pot and cover with lightly salted water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until tender, 10 to 15 minutes; drain.
Whisk oil, vinegar, basil, mustard, salt, and black pepper together in a large bowl. Add potatoes and onion; toss gently to coat. Set aside until cool, about 30 minutes.
Fold blue cheese and chives into potato salad until blended.

raw_recipe.headline: Picnic Potato Salad with No Mayonnaise
raw_recipe.description: This picnic potato salad with no mayonnaise recipe folds in tangy blue cheese, onion, and chives at the end, which creates an exciting flavor profile.

review.reviewBody: I am so excited to be the first person to review this recipe! This potato salad is not a 'traditional' recipe, but I think that works in its favor. I loved the tangy flavor of the vinegar, and the little bit of spice the mustard gave the salad. And the blue cheese just put this over the top. I will definitely be making this again because it was so easy to make and tasted wonderful. Thanks for sharing the recipe, Maridele!

Our neighborhood potluck during the Memorial Day weekend was a perfect opportunity to make potato salad. I truly dislike potato salads made with mayonnaise, so I decided to try this one. It was unbelievably delicious! I made a few changes. Rather than boil the potatoes, I quartered, oiled (olive oil) and roasted them in a preheated oven for 30 minutes at 400°. I removed them from the oven before they got mushy and let them cool down before proceeding. I substituted a little red wine vinegar for some of the balsamic since I have a VERY thick, syrupy balsamic that tends to be very sweet. I used Trader Joe's Aioli garlic mustard. I wanted a salad with a bit more crunch, so I increased the amounts of the red onion, and I also added half of a large red bell pepper, chopped. I added 2 tablespoons of chopped parsley to the basil and chives…and I doubled the amount of basil in the recipe. Finally, I substituted Trader Joe's crumbled goat cheese for the blue cheese. Wonderful blend of sweetness from the balsamic, heat from the black pepper & mustard, crunch from the red onion and bell pepper, and tang from the goat cheese. I'm going to make this for the Fourth of July!

It was well received by all the ladies at our lunch. I would like the look of it better with white balsamic but didn't have any on hand. I added a couple tablespoons of capers and a little of the brine. Used Feta Cheese and green onions (because that's what I had on hand) and it was terrific. I also microwaved the potatoes the second time I made it and they were much nicer.

I would make this again with the following changes. Use white balsamic vinegar so your salad looks like the one in the picture. Mine turned out to be a very unappetizing brown color since I used regular balsamic as stated in the recipe. I would also wait to add the fresh basil along with the chives right before serving. My basil wilted as I added it to the warm potatoes along with the dressing as stated in the recipe. You will not be disappointed after making these corrections.

This is my go-to summer side salad and always a huge hit with guests big and small. I’ve substituted feta for the blue cheese and usually pass on chives. And I typically make a few hours (or the day before) to help the dressing soak in even more. So so good.

I loved it and so did my family. THey asked for it again, just two days after having it! I didn't add as much Balsamic Vin.- I added 3/4 to 1 Tbsp, and rather than adding Blue Cheese, I left that out and added 1/4 c. Miracle Whip, with 1/2tsp Original(unsalted) Mrs.Dash, and because we like our food with a bit of heat, I added 1/8tsp. powdered Cayenne Pepper! I diced up one Stalk of celery You can use 2 if you want) and I added 2 Hard boiled Eggs, cut up finely, and mixed throughout! So good. THanks for posting this recipe though, it gave me something to work with, as I like to be creative.

We all liked this. I cooked the potatoes in the microwave, stirring a couple of times, rather than boiling (about 9 min in mine). I used dried chives because I didn't have fresh and used regular reds chopped to approximate quartered new potatoes but otherwise made no changes. Served at room temp as suggested and the only change I would make is to try lessening the oil a tad next time, but that may not work. They weren't too oily, I just tend to reduce the amount we use as much as possible. We rarely use mayo so it's nice to have another variation on one of our favorites. This is a very bold flavor though so I don't know that it is as versatile as some salads. I think it would be a nice compliment to a simple grilled steak.

I made this recipe as is. It very good and tasty, but next time i'll be making it with white balsamic, the potatoes were dark brown color ,it did not look very appetizing. So for that I will give it 3stars.

Great salad. I have been enjoying a variation of same potato salad recipe for many years courtesy of my German Mother-in law and now my wife makes it. We make it frequently. Differences are small and optional. Mother-in law would coarsely chop several dill pickles to add along with a good dose of the dill pickle juice. Lots of coarse ground black pepper. She used cider vinegar, I've used balsamic, love both. We also will eat it hot. Makes great sandwiches using fresh hard rolls. Shredded hard boiled eggs or pickled eggs are a must. Make a day ahead and refrigerate for better flavor. My wife was raised on this, it's great! A little touch of fresh ground horseradish is a great option also.

This is an extremely delicious recipe. I really love the mayo type potato salads- but wanted a change-and had a party of people with sophisticated palates, Plus I had an abundance of fresh basil and chives in my garden. Here are some tips for a perfect outcome. You really have to watch the cooking time. If the potatoes over cook, they will break down to mush, like mashed potatoes, so depending on how large your cubes are, they need to come out as soon as its soft enough to eat. They need to have plenty of firmness to withstand the mixing. My cubes were approx. an inch in diameter and they were done in 10 minutes. After they cool down to the point where they aren't profusely steaming, you need to coat them with the wet dressing, this will help stop the sticky characteristics that potatoes get as they cool. I would also wait to add the blue cheese until serving. Cheese can start to get runny if mixed in. There are similar recipes on this site that add celery and pickle, and I think that would ruin this elegant and tasty dish that has such great flavors and sophistication without being too complicated.
Felt the amount of bluecheese was a little much. Going to remake using half the amount in the recipe

This is a good recipe! I was excited to find a recipe that wasn't goopy with mayo; although I do like mayo, it just doesn't hold up well. This is a keeper, and can be modified somewhat. I used feta cheese and a mixture of regular and Dijon mustards. Had compliments!
It was too bold a flavor with the balsamic --I will not make again.
I like that there isn’t mayonnaise. It’s a great alternative. The flavors all work well together, no ingredient is overpowering.
Everyone Loved it!! Used feta instead of blue cheese just because that’s what I had and it was really great.
I didn’t have any blue cheese on hand but was still very good without it. Will try with the blue cheese next time, and maybe some crispy bacon for texture.
Really good. Nice break from mayonnaise. I used Feta cheese as I didn’t have blue cheese. It was perfect, will probably make it again soon.
Very easy to make and tasty. Just a note about the vinegar....best to use white balsamic vinegar.
We used golden balsamic vinegar and the rest if the recipe as written. We love this lower calorie version.
Great just as described. We had difficulty crumbling the cheese but a fork helped immeasurably. Might try olives in place of cheese.
